`./compile.sh` reports **`compiled OK`**.

I wrote `tests/org/apache/commons/lang3/SerializationUtilsAgentTest.java` — a self-contained JUnit 4 test class (matching the `junit-4.12` jar in `lib/`), with all fixtures defined inline.

Coverage, all anchored to the javadoc contract in `api/`:

**`serialize(Serializable)` → `byte[]`**
- returns a non-null, non-empty array; round-trips to an `equals` but non-identical object
- `null` object → still returns bytes that deserialize back to `null` (sibling two-arg form documents "may be null")
- non-serializable member field → `SerializationException`, asserted to be a `RuntimeException` (the documented "(runtime)")

**`serialize(Serializable, OutputStream)`**
- bytes written are deserializable back to the original
- stream is closed afterward — verified with a `ByteArrayOutputStream` subclass that records `close()`
- `null` stream → `IllegalArgumentException`; `null` object accepted; bad object → `SerializationException`

**`deserialize(byte[])` / `deserialize(InputStream)`**
- round-trip equality; each call yields a fresh, independent graph
- `InputStream` form closes the stream — verified with a close-recording `ByteArrayInputStream`
- `null` input → `IllegalArgumentException`; empty array and garbage bytes → `SerializationException`

**`clone(T)`**
- returns `equals` but non-identical instance; deep — nested mutable list is a separate copy and unaffected by later mutation of the source
- `clone(null)` → `null`
- non-serializable member → `SerializationException` (runtime)
- collections, primitive arrays, and object arrays clone to detached equal copies
- primitive type tokens (`byte.class` … `void.class`) survive a deep clone as the same canonical `Class` object, plus a byte-array round-trip of `int.class`
